title: Year 12 Investigating Science Module 7 – Fact or Fallacy?
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Investigating Science Module 7, organised by its five Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

categories.name: How can a claim be tested?

questions.prompt: What quality asks whether an investigation actually tests the claim it is meant to test?
What quality asks whether repeated results are consistent?
What quality asks how close measurements are to an accepted value?
What type of error varies unpredictably between repeated measurements?
What type of error consistently biases measurements in one direction?

categories.name: What affects how data are interpreted?

questions.prompt: What inactive treatment is used as a comparison in many clinical trials?
What trial design keeps both participants and researchers unaware of treatment allocation?
What comparison group does not receive the experimental treatment?
What factor can distort data when financial interests influence research?
What term describes deliberately presenting statistics in a misleading way?
questions.answer: Statistical manipulation. Accept: manipulation of statistics.

categories.name: What evidence is needed for valid conclusions?

questions.prompt: What term describes a relationship between two variables that change together?
What term means that one factor produces a change in another?
Does correlation by itself prove causation?
What effect occurs when people change their behaviour because they know they are being observed?
What term describes evidence that can be repeatedly obtained with consistent results?

categories.name: How does science reporting shape public understanding?

questions.prompt: What type of journal article has been evaluated by other experts before publication?
What term describes a financial or personal interest that may bias scientific reporting?
What effect occurs when a positive impression of a person or brand influences judgement of unrelated claims?
What term describes a claim presented as scientific but lacking reliable scientific methods or evidence?
Astrology, numerology and iridology are syllabus examples of what?

categories.name: Can peer review help science find the truth?

questions.prompt: What process has other experts evaluate scientific work before or after publication?
What process repeats a study to check whether its findings can be obtained again?
What term describes intentionally inventing or altering research results?
What phrase describes pressure on researchers to produce frequent publications?
What type of journal may imitate legitimate scholarly publishing while providing little or no genuine peer review?
questions.answer: A predatory journal. Accept: fake science journal.

finalRound.prompt: What key distinction must be demonstrated before a correlation can be claimed as a cause-and-effect relationship?
